tickets.title: Story playback: native timeline and scheduled visuals
tickets.body:

Why now: The Vinyl Cosmos prototype needs repeatable beat iteration without numbered transport sliders or waiting through the whole sequence.

Scope: Scene-owned stories; separate story and animation clocks; explicit seek capability; stable beat identities; persisted story authoring; guarded transport commands. Later scheduled visual overlap/preparation/disposal follows the same model. Playback speed and Resolume story integration remain design-only.

Delivery: Substantial end-to-end slices, with review and real isolated-app validation inside each ticket. First demonstration migrates a copy of Vinyl Cosmos; protect the user's current session and saved original.

IMPLEMENTATION AUTHORIZED: User said Start implementing on 17 September 2026. Preserve prerequisites and independent review.

- Keep clip dimensions fixed during recording and handle stop, cancellation, runtime replacement and app close without corrupting existing files.
- Demonstrate still and video capture in the actual app. Verify decoded dimensions and clip playback, including a preview smaller than the output resolution.
Checklist: implementation; focused checks; independent code/UI review; integration; real capture demonstration.

tickets.title: Turn the footer into a compact actionable status bar
tickets.body:
Problem: The footer mostly repeats static information. Build activity and faults require a large Jobs & diagnostics pane.

User result: Read useful build, problem, and runtime/connection status in a compact VS Code-style footer. Open the relevant details by clicking or using the keyboard.

Acceptance:
- Replace the static footer content with current build activity, problem counts, and useful runtime/connection health from existing authoritative state.
- Keep idle status concise. Do not invent progress percentages or report stale failures as current.
- Make each actionable status item open or focus its corresponding detail view. Reopen a closed detail pane when needed.

# C02 proposal: one executable component through the existing worker

Status: planning-only proposal for coordinator review, 13 September 2026 UTC.
No implementation or graphics validation has occurred. C01 implementation is
owned by `/root/component_metadata`; this proposal does not edit its files or the
tracked architecture/plan. Read its final integrated exports before dispatch.

## Recommendation and consequential options

**Recommend C02 as an internal executable bridge:** add SDK `0.3.0`, compiled
artifact `artifactVersion: 4` and linked envelope `linkedVersion: 4`, execute a
single declared image-source component in the actual existing visual-worker path,
and test that path with fake renderer/device resources. Keep ordinary Studio/MCP
supported SDKs at `0.1.0`/`0.2.0` and preserve strict product admission. C04 later
opens the authoring path after integration and serialized real GPU validation.

Alternative: enable complete public single-component Studio authoring in C02.
This immediately needs source-editor, scene-save format, control UI/client guards,
discovery, installed/export rejection and GPU acceptance changes. It is coherent
but substantially larger and competes with filesystem integration. Defer it to
C04/C05. A metadata-only compiler implementation without worker execution is not
the recommended C02 outcome: the proposed worker tests must run the real entry.

The bridge admits **no inputs and exactly one output named `image`**, with C01's
linear-sRGB/premultiplied image declaration. Number/live controls may be empty.
Both existing state declarations (`stateless`/`stateful`, reset by seed) are
admitted; a private factory owns state. Other valid C01 metadata remains valid
catalog data but is rejected for this executable profile. No event, signal-input,
effect-input, arbitrary image allocation or graph scheduler is claimed.

This is one additive branch in the existing selector/compiler/linker/worker,
not a second compiler service, scene store or runtime authority. SDK 0.3 may be
compiled by internal development/test callers; that does not mean ordinary
Studio, project files or installed releases support it. Do not publish 0.3 in
`studioCapabilities` or `discoverVisualSdk().supportedSdkVersions` in this slice.
The project-v1 capability gate below is a prerequisite in the same reviewed C02
integration that widens internal source admission; global SDK validation alone
must not silently widen persisted project metadata.

## Observed owners and why both discriminants are necessary

- `source-policy.mjs` calls `sdkSourceFile`; source envelopes and SDK version are
  separate. 0.2 already accepts legacy source envelopes and explicit assets v2.
- `worker.mjs` currently parses 0.2 literal `defineVisual`, copies selected SDK
  types, emits `__lux/sdk.js`/`__lux/parameters.js`, inventories dependency hashes
  and constructs the artifact through `artifactBody`.
- `artifact-identity.mjs` admits only artifact/linked versions 2/3 (or implicit v1),
  seals control fields only at v3, and hard-codes v3 to SDK 0.2. Its strict owner
  cannot accept component metadata under an old discriminant without changing
  the meaning and hash body of the existing format.
- `link-worker.mjs` re-verifies the artifact/dependency closure, restricts every
  virtual import and copies artifact fields into a separately hashed linked body.
  The browser worker gets linked code rather than the compiled module inventory,
  so component metadata must survive in a new linked v4 body as well.
- `authored-worker-assets.mjs` verifies linked data and original/derived assets
  before importing submitted code. `worker-control-state.mjs` prepares schema and
  captured-intrinsic post-import checks. Both require additive v4/component handling.
- `visual-worker.mjs` owns clock, seeded RNG, update/render cadence, the one output
  RenderTarget, queue completion, capture and final presentation. Reuse those.
- `standalone-client.ts`, `service-client.ts`, `control-state.ts` and
  `capabilities.ts` still model only SDK 0.1/0.2. Their ordinary admission must not
  accidentally treat 0.3 as legacy when the general SourceBundle union expands.
- `scene-document.ts` preserves scene versions 1/2/3. Export and installed readers
  interpret linked v3 as parameter release v2 and must reject v4 explicitly until
  their later closure/capability work is implemented.
- The actual first installed/transport reader is
  `tools/gpu-spike/transport-release.cjs::readTransportRelease`. Its policy calls
  `runtime-validation.mjs`'s reexport of shared `linkedBody`; rebuilding that
  policy will recognize v4. Add a reader-local allowlist admitting only implicit
  linked v1 and explicit v2/v3 **before** calling the shared validator. Do not
  rely on a stale generated policy or `runtime-capability.cjs`, which only checks
  build markers and does not receive a linked envelope.

## Exact source, artifact and linked contract

Keep SourceBundle envelopes unchanged: implicit v1 or explicit `sourceVersion:2`
with exact current assets. Add SDK `0.3.0` only as a new source SDK discriminant.
For 0.3, `sourceArtifactVersion` always returns 4, including code-only/no-assets
source. Asset limits/codecs, source limits and allowed bare imports stay unchanged.

Define compiled v4 as the existing asset-bearing base fields plus exactly:

```ts
{
  artifactVersion: 4;
  sdkVersion: '0.3.0';
  executionModel: 'single-image-source-v1';
  component: ComponentMetadata; // normalized C01 declarationVersion: 1
  componentMetadataHash: Hash;
  controls: ControlSchema;
  controlSchemaHash: Hash;
}
```

`componentMetadataHash = SHA256(UTF8(canonicalComponentMetadataJson(component)))`.
The existing control hash remains SHA256 of existing canonicalControlSchemaJson.

its epoch is active, then close it in `finally`, including exceptions. On failure

returns invalid output, the bridge still owns that pending backend operation.

await/settle the tracked operation (record rejection without losing the original

or renderer teardown; a settled JavaScript render promise alone is insufficient.

termination fallback; do not free still-used resources merely because evaluation
was rejected or a timeout elapsed. No unbounded orderly-drain guarantee is claimed.

target, await its existing queue-completion barrier and emit a new completed frame.

tickets.title: Save and recall named looks in Studio
tickets.body:
Save named looks and recall them in Studio.

User result: Save the working visual as a named look. Find it again in a compact Looks browser and load it with its controls and animation settings intact.

First delivery:
- Reuse the existing verified scene document and source bundle. A look includes the accepted source, assets, component values, LFO settings, and supported output settings. It is a self-contained snapshot; library updates must not silently change a saved look.
- Add Save Look to the normal creative workflow. Use a short name field and show a thumbnail when a fresh capture is available. A capture failure must not lose a valid saved look.
- List named looks in a small browser with an explicit Load action. Reuse the existing profile-local durable store and scene admission patterns where possible. Keep look storage separate from workspace layouts and the component library.
- Do not silently replace an existing look with the same name. Support Save as new and an explicit update of the selected look.
- Preserve unsaved source and control edits before loading another look. Use the existing dirty-document guard or a recoverable draft, not silent overwrite.
- Load through the existing validated build/activation path. A failed or incompatible look keeps the previous working preview and its controls. Report the failure clearly.
- Demonstrate save, changed controls/LFO, recall, restart and recall again, two distinct looks, and failed-load retention. Include nested components when LUX-117 is integrated.
- Capture actual normal/narrow UI screenshots. Complete independent UX, source, data-protection and resource-cleanup review before landing.

Design direction: a saved look is a complete visual snapshot. Parameter-only presets cannot recreate a look after the source changes; defer them until actual use needs them. Reuse scene persistence rather than introduce another source format.

Delivery checklist: inspect existing Save/Open and storage; short independent design critique; implement; demonstrate; review; integrate. User authorized this feature for implementation overnight with routine design decisions delegated.

tickets.title: Draft Pigment Rivers painting components for later testing
tickets.body:
# Pigment Rivers — reference analysis and blind source draft

User request: analyze the second painting reference and build corresponding
components, continuing the source-only worktree workflow. No compilation,
execution, preview, or tests until a later agent is authorized to perform them.

## Reference analysis, ranked by payoff for effort

| Priority | Piece | Reuse and smallest useful addition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Broad flowing pink, green, yellow and cyan pigment bands | New folded scalar field for elongated bands. Organic Regions favors compact lobes, so keep it intact and use its LoRegion consumer convention. |
| 2 | Uneven dark ink seams | Reuse Organic Boundary Ink's ornament output against the new field's estimated edge distance. |
| 3 | Dragged dry-brush marks and paper tooth | New reusable image-input Dry Brush & Paper overlay. Use stationary fibers and a small directional sampling offset to suggest underpaint showing through. |
| 4 | Pale translucent pools and pooled edges | Reuse Animated Watercolor's ornament field for wash variation, blended with a dedicated acid-green/hot-pink palette. |
| 5 | Nested blue/green contour scribbles | Reuse Nested Contours in selected quiet regions, with the same LoRegion local frame. |
| 6 | Splattered edges / studio-paper margin | Add optional seeded flecks and a rough paper margin to the surface overlay. This references the photographed artwork without requiring its photograph as a texture. |

Motion should slowly fold and stretch the pigment masses while the paper stays
still. Avoid rainbow cycling, glossy shading, or fast global wobble. Dark seams
and negative space matter as much as the vivid palette. This is a procedural
interpretation, not a reconstruction of the exact brush strokes or a fluid simulation.

## Implementation plan

1. Add Folded Pigment Bands as a shader-field provider: analytic large folds,
   edge distances, tangent/local frames, shape controls and stable identities.
2. Add a compatible Pigment River renderer using the existing phrasing, wash,
   boundary and contour providers through source imports; leave their source unchanged.
3. Add a separate Dry Brush & Paper image effect with grain, scumble, bristles,
   optional margin and flecks. Wire a runnable SDK 0.4 composition.
4. Write CPU contract tests and a complete source-bundle recipe for the next agent.

Acceptance for this task is source authoring and handoff only. Independent code
review, successful compilation, actual UI evidence, performance, control checks,
save/reopen and invalid-edit preservation remain deferred and unverified.

tickets.title: Reclaim default workspace space from Jobs and Diagnostics
tickets.body:
Problem: The Jobs & diagnostics pane occupies default workspace space even when idle or repeating information suitable for the footer.

User result: Gain space for Preview and Source by using compact footer summaries, opening Jobs/Diagnostics details only when needed.

Acceptance:
- Once the C19 status bar and its detail navigation are usable, remove the idle Jobs/Diagnostics pane from the default workspace layout.
- Keep Jobs and Diagnostics available through normal pane controls and status-bar actions. Preserve docking, dragging, resizing, tabs, close/reopen, and saved layouts.
- Preserve existing user-saved layouts rather than silently removing deliberately placed panes. A fresh or reset default layout should provide the space-saving arrangement.
- Build/runtime failures remain visible through the status bar when details are closed. Opening details must reveal the relevant information.
- Demonstrate a fresh/reset layout, a build failure with details closed, reopening via the footer, closing again, and restoring a saved layout with the pane deliberately open.

Why now: Direct user feedback says the large job/diagnostics panel takes space for information that could be small in the footer. This completes the visible workspace benefit of C19.

Sequence: Deliver after the companion ticket to turn the footer into a working status bar. Retain detail access before changing defaults.
